extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline (practitioners of record)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural requirements, and sanctions governing registered patent practitioners' conduct before the USPTO, including withdrawal obligations, signature rules, response to show-cause orders, cooperation with investigations, and possible discipline/sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: As a registered practitioner, Respondent is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered patent attorneys and agents must follow the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct in all matters before the Office; those rules form the baseline standards for evaluating practitioner behavior in disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO disciplinary jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner discipline pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters involving alleged misconduct by registered practitioners are adjudicated under these statutes and regulations; practitioners should expect proceedings and sanctions under this authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of representation obligation (37 C.F.R. § 11.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must take reasonable steps to withdraw from representation when appropriate; failing to take reasonable steps to withdraw constitutes a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a practitioner decides not to continue representation (e.g., after learning of potentially improper conduct by others), the practitioner must timely and properly withdraw rather than remain practitioner of record while refusing to act. Failure to withdraw can support disciplinary charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the integrity of the USPTO process (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not engage in conduct adversely affecting the integrity of the USPTO patent application process; failure to withdraw or comply with withdrawal rules can constitute such conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions or omissions that undermine the integrity of proceedings (including procedural noncompliance that leads to improperly-signed filings) may be charged under § 11.804(d) and result in discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal withdrawal procedure and change of correspondence (37 C.F.R. § 1.36(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who withdraws must file a 'Request for Withdrawal as Attorney or Agent and Change of Correspondence Address' as required by 37 C.F.R. § 1.36(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely declining to represent a client without filing the required withdrawal/change-of-address form is improper; failure to file the form was cited as an element of misconduct in these proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and who may sign filings (37 C.F.R. § 1.33(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies and other filings must be signed by an authorized registered practitioner; signing by an officer or manager of a juristic entity applicant in place of a registered practitioner violated 37 C.F.R. § 1.33(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improperly signed responses (e.g., by unregistered persons) violate signature rules and can lead to termination of proceedings; practitioners of record have responsibility to ensure filings comply with signature requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to USPTO show cause orders
rubrics_metrics.description: When the USPTO issues show cause orders requiring applicants to show cause why proceedings should not be terminated, the practitioner of record receives the orders and is implicated in ensuring proper response or withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner who receives show cause orders must either timely and properly respond (consistent with rules) or withdraw in accordance with applicable regulations; failure to do so may lead to termination of the underlying proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for improperly signed filings — termination of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Improperly signed responses to show cause orders can result in final orders terminating the proceedings in the affected patent applications (example: termination in all 136 applications here).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may terminate prosecution in applications where filings are not properly signed or authorized; such consequences are among the substantive harms the rules seek to prevent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available and imposed for practitioner misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary measures include public reprimand, probation, and suspension (up to 30 days) among other remedies; the Final Order publicly reprimanded the Respondent and imposed six months' probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may be tailored to the misconduct and informed by mitigating/aggravating factors; an Order to Show Cause and further proceedings may be used to impose suspension if probation conditions are violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation enforcement procedure (Order to Show Cause and suspension process)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause and may request the USPTO Director to enter an order suspending the Respondent for up to thirty (30) days; Respondent has fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure includes service of the Order to Show Cause at the address of record, a 15-day response period, consideration of any response, and possible referral to the USPTO Director for immediate suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of disciplinary orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director will electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary outcomes are publicly available; notices include factual summary, the nature of the violations, and imposed discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to cooperate with inquiries into third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall cooperate fully with the USPTO in any present or future inquiry into any third-party entities or persons involved in reviewing, preparing, signing, filing, or arranging for the filings at issue (e.g., foreign representatives or associates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation includes providing information about third parties such as foreign associates or entities soliciting or providing work; noncooperation can influence further discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating and aggravating factors considered in discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors such as lack of prior discipline, acknowledgment of ethical lapses, genuine contrition, acceptance of responsibility, and exceptional cooperation with OED's investigation were noted as considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated contrition and cooperation can mitigate sanction severity; prior disciplinary history or failure to cooperate can aggravate discipline and be used in future proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial/educational steps and review of guidance materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent certified that he watched USPTO materials on 'Patents priorities for FY2025 and fraud and threat mitigation' and reviewed applicable MPEP provisions (e.g., MPEP § 2223) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.116 concerning withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing USPTO guidance and MPEP provisions is an appropriate remedial step after misconduct; such actions may be included in settlement terms or considered favorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights in settlement agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the settlement, Respondent waived the right to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, review under § 11.57, and the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements resolving disciplinary matters may include waivers of appellate and reconsideration rights; practitioners should be aware of such consequences when agreeing to terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for additional discrete discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prevents the OED Director from seeking discrete discipline for any misconduct that formed the basis for an Order to Show Cause issued during probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where a settlement provides specific sanctions, separate or additional disciplinary actions may later be pursued for discrete misconduct arising from the same facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements — address of record for service (37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders (e.g., Order to Show Cause) shall be sent to Respondent at the last address of record furnished pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must maintain accurate addresses of record to receive official communications; failure to do so has procedural implications for service and response deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of disciplinary record on future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of this disciplinary proceeding when addressing future complaints or in future disciplinary proceedings against the Respondent as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's prior disciplinary record can be used against them in subsequent matters and may influence severity of future sanctions.
